title: Trump vs. America
text:
If Donald Trump has maintained one pretense continuously throughout his career in politics, it is that his entire goal is to help the United States of America. The founding conceit of the first Trump campaign was that he would set aside his business interests, at great personal expense, to rescue the country he loved. It was embedded in his slogans (“America First,” “Make America Great Again”) and his palace-building binge, which he naturally justified as his service to the symbols of the country. He hugged flags .

 Finally, at a press conference this afternoon, he broke character.

 The CNN reporter Kaitlan Collins asked the president a question about his comment earlier this week to Vladimir Putin. Seeing the Russian dictator, Trump broke into a wide smile, perhaps a more genuine expression of delight than he has ever displayed before in public, and called Putin “my friend.” Collins asked Trump, “You said Putin is your friend. Russia, of course, is Iran’s biggest ally. Do you believe Putin is a friend to America?”

 Trump replied:

 “I can’t speak to America. I’ve been dealing with Putin during the fake Russia, Russia, Russia hoax, and to be honest, he was very nice about it. It was a rigged hoax. It was a hoax that was made up by the Democrats. It probably helped me win the election—re-win the election.”

 Even by Trumpian standards, this was an extraordinary confession.

 First, he said he cannot speak for what is good for America, as if the United States were some foreign entity with interests totally inscrutable to him. He then explained that Putin is very good to him personally. Any other world leader caught using covert measures to help a pro-Russian candidate win the American presidency would apparently have been cross, but Putin was “very nice about it,” which just shows what a swell guy he is.

 [ Philips Payson O’Brien: Trump’s axis of ignorance ] 

 Recall that the Trumpian line has always been that Trump sides with Russia so frequently because he is coldly looking out for the American wallet. Last year, Trump batted away a reporter’s question about his tilt toward Russia by saying, “I’m not aligned with Putin. I’m not aligned with anybody. I’m aligned with the United States of America and for the good of the world.” This week, after Trump’s display of warmth and love toward Putin, J. D. Vance posted a clip of the encounter and commented on X, “The president will talk to anyone, anywhere, to advocate for American interests.”

 It was obvious enough, given that Trump had called in to a meeting of Europeans who were supporting Ukraine to urge them to stop doing so. Trump “told Ukraine’s European allies on Thursday they could save money as well as lives by ending the war with Russia, according to five European officials who were briefed on the discussion,” Politico reported . The White House denies this.

 Trump has always claimed to oppose sending aid to Ukraine because he resents sending American money overseas. But his effort to persuade Europeans to stop aiding Ukraine suggests that his actual motivation is that he wants Russia to win because he admires and sympathizes with its leader, his personal friend. “America First” has always meant Trump first.
